question: A nurse wants to make sure new health posters are clear before printing thousands of copies. What should she do?

question: What is the main goal of Universal Child Immunization?

options.A: Treating chronic illnesses in school-aged children

question: Which medication group is commonly given to treat roundworms by paralyzing them so the body can pass them out?

question: What is the main benefit of building muscle strength around a joint?

question: What is the primary position of the nurse in adolescent healthcare delivery?

options.A: Frontline gateway and trusted counselor

question: Why is taking Parkinson's medication right on time, every single day, so important?

options.A: Delayed timing makes the medication completely toxic to the kidneys.

question: How is pharmacodynamics different from pharmacokinetics?

options.B: Pharmacodynamics only applies to herbal remedies, whereas pharmacokinetics applies to synthetic drugs

question: A nurse working in a rural primary health clinic notices an increase in skin infections among children. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Close the clinic permanently until a modern hospital is built nearby

question: When is the right time to chart an injection you just gave your patient?

options.D: Immediately after giving the injection

question: Who is the main pioneer associated with scientific management theory?

options.A: Florence Nightingale

question: What are the two core behavioral areas used to understand autism?

options.A: Aggressive outbursts and profound sleepiness
options.B: Social communication challenges and repetitive behaviors
options.C: Hyperactivity and attention deficits
options.D: Memory loss and sudden physical paralysis

question: A patient tells a nurse they only take 'natural' painkillers bought off the supermarket shelf. What is the best nursing action?

options.B: Ignore the information since a prescription was not required

question: What is the core belief behind quantitative research?

options.A: A single objective reality exists that can be measured
options.B: Reality is entirely subjective and changes for every person
options.C: Facts only matter if the patient agrees with the nurse
options.D: There is no truth, only personal opinions in healthcare

explanation: Quantitative research assumes there is a clear, measurable truth out there waiting to be discovered with the right tools.

question: Which part of a child's bone allows it to grow longer as they get older?

options.A: Periosteum

question: Which injection is routinely given to every newborn baby to prevent dangerous bleeding?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Iron drops
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Folic acid

question: What is the medical term when individual cells grow larger in size?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Think 'hyper' (more/bigger) and 'trophy' (growth). Hypertrophy means the cells are getting bigger, not multiplying!

question: When is Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) most often used during fertility treatments?

options.A: When the female partner has irregular menstrual cycles
options.B: To prevent the transmission of common seasonal flus
options.C: Severe male factor infertility with very low sperm count
options.D: When the couple prefers natural conception at home

explanation: ICSI is a neat lab trick where embryologists inject a single, healthy sperm straight into an egg to bypass severe male fertility hurdles.

question: Which factor is most strongly tied to whether a woman uses modern contraception?

options.A: Age of the youngest grandparent
options.B: Employment in the banking sector
options.C: Level of formal education
options.D: Proximity to major airports

explanation: Studies consistently show that women with more formal education are better equipped to make informed choices and utilize modern family planning.

question: How is Type 2 diabetes different from Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Type 2 requires immediate lifelong oral medication without dietary changes
options.B: Type 2 is strictly an acute condition that resolves without long-term treatment
options.C: Type 2 only affects elderly patients who have a family history of kidney disease
options.D: Type 2 involves insulin resistance and relative deficiency rather than total destruction

question: Which of the following describes the main characteristic feature of pertussis infection?

options.A: Persistent watery diarrhea lasting several weeks
options.B: Violent and uncontrollable coughing spells
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.D: Stiff jaw muscles and painful body spasms

question: What is the main goal of therapeutic phlebotomy in polycythaemia?

options.A: To increase blood pressure
options.B: To remove excess white blood cells
options.C: To provide iron for the liver
options.D: To reduce red blood cell mass and hematocrit

question: What is the main purpose of filing a separate internal incident report after an adverse event?

options.A: To track systemic trends and guide organizational safety improvements
options.B: To increase the patient's monthly hospital billing charges
options.C: To provide immediate grounds for terminating the involved nurse
options.D: To publish the staff member's name publicly in local newspapers

explanation: Exactly! Incident reports help management figure out why errors happen so the hospital can fix underlying processes and stop them from happening again.

question: What is the main difference in who goes into quarantine versus isolation?

options.A: Quarantine requires a hospital bed, while isolation happens at home
options.B: Quarantine is for sick patients, while isolation is for healthy travelers
options.C: Quarantine is for exposed healthy people, while isolation is for sick people
options.D: Quarantine is voluntary, while isolation is always forced by law

explanation: The core difference lies in the health status of the person: exposed-yet-healthy for quarantine, and actively ill for isolation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is a key part of emergency preparedness in a home care plan?

options.A: Disconnecting all medical equipment to save electricity
options.B: Waiting for the annual checkup to report severe symptoms
options.C: Knowing who to call and what steps to take during a sudden crisis
options.D: Relying solely on neighbors for medical decisions

explanation: When an emergency strikes, panic shouldn't take over. Having a clear plan of who to call keeps both the patient and family safe.

question: What happens inside red blood cells to cause those sudden, recurring fever spikes in malaria?

options.A: The rapid multiplication and bursting of red blood cells
options.B: The sudden drop in total white blood cell production
options.C: The allergic reaction to mosquito saliva in the skin
options.D: The physical blocking of large arteries in the heart

explanation: Well done! As the parasites multiply and burst out of red blood cells, they release toxins that trigger a sudden, intense fever.

question: What happens when a patient suffers from vesicoureteral reflux?

options.A: Urine flows backward from the bladder up into the ureters
options.B: Stones form rapidly inside the lower bladder cavity
options.C: Blood enters the urine directly from the renal artery
options.D: The ureter walls lose all smooth muscle tone permanently

explanation: You've got this! 'Reflux' simply means fluid travels the wrong way—in this case, heading back up toward the kidneys.

question: A patient with advanced cancer starts strong opioid pain medication. What preventive care must you include?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload from the oral medications
options.B: Encouraging a low-fiber diet to reduce gastrointestinal activity during treatment
options.C: Checking blood pressure every fifteen minutes to monitor for sudden hypertension
options.D: Administering prescribed stool softeners and laxatives to prevent opioid-induced constipation

question: Which of these routine ward procedures strictly requires surgical asepsis (sterile technique)?

options.A: Taking a routine blood pressure reading
options.B: Administering oral medications
options.C: Assisting a patient to brush their teeth

question: What is the main use of the Nigerian National Formulary?

question: You are assisting with a wound wash and fluid is likely to splash. What PPE do you need?

options.A: Gloves and a standard cloth surgical cap only

options.C: Sterile surgical gloves and a paper face mask only

question: What is the single most reliable way to monitor daily changes in a patient's fluid balance?

options.A: Daily body weight measurement

question: What is the correct sequence of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS)?

question: Why must nurses carefully separate normal aging from disease pathology?

question: What are the classic red flags of a thyrotoxic storm?

options.A: Dangerous high fever and rapid heart rate

question: Which body organ is mainly responsible for breaking down (metabolizing) most drugs?

options.C: The stomach

question: A patient asks why they must finish all their antibiotics even after feeling better. What is the best response?

question: Why should nurses team up with traditional and religious leaders in community campaigns against GBV?

question: A patient is shocked to test positive for Hepatitis C years after getting an unsterile injection. Why did it take so long to show up?

question: What is your immediate nursing action right after the skin snip is taken?

question: Which prenatal event is most associated with an increased risk of neurological learning differences?

question: If a patient's blood pressure drops suddenly, how does the body try to fix it right away?

question: In history, why did many Nigerian communities use facial marks?

question: What is wound dehiscence?

question: Which skin sign strongly points to a liver problem or high bilirubin levels?

question: What main technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?

question: Why is mixing minor tranquilizers with alcohol so dangerous?

question: Which type of research relies mostly on numbers and statistics?

question: What is the main job of the neurotransmitter GABA when you fall asleep?

question: How long must a seizure continue for it to be called status epilepticus?

options.B: Longer than 5 minutes
options.C: At least 60 minutes
options.D: More than 2 hours

question: What is the main purpose of using screening tools like CAGE or ASSIST in nursing?

question: A pregnant woman in a remote village has severe bleeding, but her family wastes two hours trying traditional herbs before looking for transport. Which delay has occurred?

question: What is the best dietary advice for a patient on long-term warfarin who loves green leafy vegetables?

question: A pregnant woman comes in with painless bleeding late in her pregnancy. Which action should you definitely avoid?

question: If a mother has an umbilical cord prolapse, what position should you put her in right away?

explanation: Gravity is key here! This position gets the baby's weight off the cord so oxygen can keep flowing while you prep for emergency help.

question: How does the cerebellum use an 'efference copy' during a voluntary movement?

options.A: To produce neurotransmitters required for neuromuscular transmission
options.B: To directly contract skeletal muscles without involving the cortex
options.C: To store long-term procedural memories of past movements
options.D: To compare intended motor commands with actual sensory feedback

explanation: An efference copy is like a duplicate draft of the brain's movement plan sent to the cerebellum so it can check: 'Did our body actually do what we wanted it to do?' Brilliant nursing brain at work!

question: Why do doctors often choose synergistic drug combinations?

options.A: To ensure patients spend less money at the pharmacy
options.B: To make medication administration schedules much simpler
options.C: To completely eliminate all possibilities of adverse drug reactions
options.D: To achieve a stronger therapeutic outcome than single drugs provide

explanation: Combining agents synergistically lets clinicians tackle stubborn health conditions much more effectively by boosting overall treatment power.

question: What is the primary viral cause of severe, dehydrating diarrhea in infants and young children?

options.A: Salmonella
options.B: Vibrio cholerae
options.C: Rotavirus
options.D: Entamoeba histolytica

explanation: Rotavirus is well-documented globally and locally as the most common viral pathogen responsible for severe dehydration episodes in young children. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h1)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a pregnant woman's uterus has ruptured during a difficult labor?

options.A: A gradual increase in contractions with steady pink show
options.B: Sudden sharp tearing pain and disappearance of contractions
options.C: High fever accompanied by foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: Mild lower backache that improves when walking around

explanation: If contractions suddenly stop after a sharp, tearing pain, think uterine rupture. It's a major emergency!

question: Why might you hear a systolic flow murmur in a patient with severe anemia?

options.A: Turbulent blood flow from high cardiac output
options.B: Blood leaking backward through a stiff mitral valve
options.C: Infection of the outer lining of the heart muscle
options.D: A physical hole in the ventricular septum wall

explanation: Because the heart is pumping a larger volume of blood much faster to fight the lack of oxygen, it creates a rushing, turbulent sound that we hear as a flow murmur.

question: Why should you avoid using tweezers to pull out a honeybee stinger?

options.A: Tweezers are too sharp and will cut the patient's epidermis
options.B: Squeezing can push more venom from the attached sac into the skin
options.C: It causes the stinger to dissolve inside the wound
options.D: Metal reacts chemically with insect venom to cause burns

explanation: Spot on! Pinching with tweezers squeezes the attached venom sac like a bulb syringe, pumping even more toxin straight into the patient.

question: When your brain interprets information and decides what to do about it, what is this process called?

options.A: Motor output
options.B: Hormone secretion
options.C: Integration
options.D: Sensory reception

explanation: Think of integration as your brain's processing unit making sense of all the clues it receives. Great job keeping up with your nursing studies! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the main idea behind person-centered care planning?

options.A: Allowing the nursing staff to make all daily decisions without input
options.B: Focusing solely on medical diagnoses while ignoring social history
options.C: Enforcing a strict morning schedule that all residents must follow
options.D: Tailoring care around the individual preferences and past routines of the resident

explanation: Exactly right! Person-centered care treats the resident as a unique human being, honoring their personal history and everyday preferences.

question: At what age might a nurse suspect a motor issue if an infant consistently prefers using only one hand?

options.A: By one month of age
options.B: Only during school age
options.C: Before eighteen months
options.D: Around three years old

explanation: Babies usually don't show a strong hand preference early on. Showing one-sided preference before 18 months can be an early sign of hemiplegic cerebral palsy.

question: Why is close monitoring of heart rate especially important in patients with thyroid hormone hypersecretion?

options.A: Excess hormone puts high strain on the heart, risking fast rhythms
options.B: Low heart rates always signal an emergency in endocrine disorders
options.C: Patients lose the ability to feel their own pulse in their wrists
options.D: Thyroid hormones directly damage the outer lining of the lungs

explanation: Too much thyroid hormone makes the heart work much harder, leading to rapid or irregular heartbeats that require close observation. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why do some patients with cervical ectropion report having more vaginal mucus than usual?

options.A: Bacterial vaginosis always accompanies every case of ectropion.
options.B: The vagina creates extra fluid to wash away dead squamous cells.
options.C: The columnar cells exposed on the surface produce large amounts of mucus.
options.D: The uterus is actively expelling early products of conception.

explanation: Inner columnar cells are natural mucus-makers! When they sit out on the surface, they keep doing their job, leading to a bit more discharge than normal.

question: What is the main medication given alongside other treatments for hydatid disease?

options.A: Albendazole
options.B: Aspirin
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Amoxicillin

explanation: Albendazole is the go-to antiparasitic drug used to weaken or shrink the cysts before or after surgery.

question: Why do nurse researchers rely so much on a theoretical framework?

options.A: It connects abstract nursing ideas directly to concrete patient care
options.B: It replaces the literature review section of the proposal
options.C: It guarantees that the research will be published in a journal
options.D: It eliminates the need for statistical data analysis entirely

explanation: Nursing is all about practice! Frameworks help us bridge the gap between big academic ideas and the real-world care we give patients every day.

question: Besides nerve signals, what else can trigger smooth muscle to contract?

options.A: Somatic nerve stimulation via the spinal cord
options.B: Direct voluntary relaxation exercises
options.C: Circulating hormones and local chemical changes
options.D: Conscious thoughts from the cerebral cortex

explanation: Smooth muscle is super responsive! It reacts to hormones in the blood, stretching, and local chemical shifts like oxygen or acid levels to keep your body balanced.

question: Why should we worry when livestock farmers use antibiotics too frequently?

options.A: It causes animals to stop producing milk entirely
options.B: It can contribute to antimicrobial resistance
options.C: It turns the meat a bright green color
options.D: It makes the meat taste bitter to consumers

explanation: Overusing antibiotics on animals creates tougher, resistant germs that can eventually spread to humans and shrug off our best medications.

question: What is the main job of a medication like loperamide?

options.A: Coating the stomach lining to prevent acid reflux
options.B: Stimulating water absorption by increasing salt intake
options.C: Killing all parasites living in the large intestine
options.D: Slowing down intestinal motility to reduce stool frequency

explanation: Loperamide calms down the bowel muscles (peristalsis) so a patient isn't running to the toilet quite as often. Simple and effective when used correctly!

question: How do standard clinical guidelines across a health network help patients?

options.A: It guarantees consistent quality of care regardless of which facility the patient visits
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing side effects from contraceptives
options.C: It allows nurses to perform major surgeries without physician supervision
options.D: It reduces the cost of prescription medications to zero for all citizens

explanation: Well done! Shared guidelines mean a patient gets the same safe, top-notch care whether they walk into a rural health post or a city hospital.

question: Which Nigerian law specifically tackles harmful traditional practices and gender-based violence?

options.A: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.B: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: Criminal Code for Corporate Fraud
options.D: Standard Environmental Sanitation Decree

explanation: The VAPP Act gives law enforcement a legal tool to protect people from physical, emotional, and traditional abuse, including harmful widowhood practices.

question: What must the urinary sphincters do so that normal urination can happen?

options.A: They must contract tightly
options.B: They must relax
options.C: They must spasm
options.D: They must thicken

explanation: For urine to flow out smoothly, the urinary sphincters need to open up (relax) at the same time the bladder muscle squeezes. Teamwork!

question: What is the main job of the chordae tendineae in the heart?

options.A: Carrying oxygen to the heart muscle
options.B: Creating the electrical spark for each heartbeat
options.C: Stopping the AV valves from flipping backward
options.D: Opening the valves when pressure rises

explanation: You can picture these like strong little parachute cords. They hold the valve flaps tightly in place so the heavy squeezing of the heart doesn't push them inside out!

question: What is the main difference between a hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: The patient's age and previous history of cardiac disease
options.B: The presence of acute target organ damage in emergencies
options.C: The absolute numerical reading of the diastolic blood pressure
options.D: The requirement for oral medication in emergency settings

explanation: You got it! An emergency means high blood pressure is actively damaging vital organs (like the brain or heart), whereas an urgency has high readings without active organ harm.

question: What is the normal range for intracranial pressure in adults?

options.A: 30 to 50 mmHg
options.B: 80 to 120 mmHg
options.C: 120 to 160 mmHg
options.D: 5 to 15 mmHg

explanation: Normal ICP is low, ranging between 5 and 15 mmHg. Anything persistently higher requires immediate medical and nursing intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h4)

question: What is your immediate priority action if the umbilical cord slips out (prolapses) during labor?

options.A: Manually lift the baby's head off the cord to restore blood flow
options.B: Push the visible cord gently back inside the uterine cavity
options.C: Clamp and cut the umbilical cord immediately on the spot
options.D: Instruct the mother to push as hard as she can with contractions

explanation: Keeping pressure off the cord with your hand keeps oxygen flowing to the baby while you prep for urgent delivery.

question: What type of synovial joint allows you to move your shoulder and hip in almost every direction?

options.A: Ball-and-socket joint
options.B: Pivot joint
options.C: Hinge joint
options.D: Plane joint

explanation: Right on! Ball-and-socket joints (like your shoulder and hip) give you the widest range of motion in all directions.

question: Which healthcare indicator looks at the physical setup, equipment, and staffing levels of a ward?

options.A: Process indicator
options.B: Outcome indicator
options.C: Balancing indicator
options.D: Structure indicator

explanation: Structure indicators look at the 'building blocks' or setup you have ready—like staff numbers, beds, and equipment available to deliver care.

question: What does MODS stand for in the context of prolonged shock?

options.A: Massive Oxygen Deprivation State
options.B: Multi-Organ Dysfunction Syndrome
options.C: Myocardial Obstruction Disease Syndrome
options.D: Metabolic Overload and Destruction System

explanation: MODS refers to the progressive failure of two or more organ systems resulting from severe, uncorrected systemic shock. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h9)

question: How does the respiratory system respond if blood pH drops and the body becomes too acidic?

options.A: Decreases the rate and depth of breathing
options.B: Increases the rate and depth of breathing
options.C: Stops breathing completely for short intervals
options.D: Retains all available oxygen in the alveoli

explanation: When blood is too acidic, you breathe faster and deeper to blow off excess carbon dioxide ($CO_2$). Since $CO_2$ acts as an acid, getting rid of it raises the pH back up!

question: Which type of nutrient requires the most energy for the body to break down and process?

options.A: Dietary fats
options.B: Protein
options.C: Simple sugars
options.D: Water

explanation: Protein is tough work for the gut! It takes way more metabolic effort to process protein than it does for fats or simple carbs.

question: Why is batch cooking recommended as part of a family meal strategy?

options.A: It permanently eliminates the need to store food in a refrigerator
options.B: It ensures that all food cooked is consumed in one sitting
options.C: It provides quick, healthy meals for busy days and reduces reliance on fast food
options.D: It allows the cook to avoid washing dishes for an entire month

explanation: Preparing larger portions ahead of time saves valuable time on hectic days and prevents impulsive, less nutritious food choices. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h4)

question: What is the number one risk factor for developing a placenta accreta?

options.A: A history of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Previous uterine surgery or cesarean section
options.C: Eating a high-fat diet during pregnancy
options.D: Advanced maternal age over 40 years

question: During embryonic development, which structures form the female reproductive tract, including the fallopian tubes?

options.A: Ovarian cords
options.B: Urogenital sinus
options.C: Müllerian ducts
options.D: Wolffian ducts

explanation: The Müllerian ducts are the embryonic building blocks for the female reproductive system. If they don't develop quite right, it can lead to tubal or uterine variations.

question: What is the medical term for fluid volume deficit (low fluid volume)?

options.A: Hypervolemia
options.B: Hypovolemia
options.C: Edema
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Well done! 'Hypo' means low and 'volemia' relates to blood volume. Put them together and you have hypovolemia!

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand local customs when caring for pregnant women in their communities?

options.A: To replace all standard medical textbooks with local folklore
options.B: To avoid performing physical examinations on pregnant women
options.C: To respect local beliefs while gently correcting harmful traditional practices
options.D: To force every patient to adopt Western cultural habits immediately

explanation: You got it! Respecting culture builds trust, making it easier to guide mothers away from unsafe cultural practices with love and patience.

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of secondary prevention in respiratory health?

options.A: Finding small pulmonary nodules on routine diagnostic imaging
options.B: Reversing the genetic mutations that cause inherited lung disorders
options.C: Identifying early airway obstruction using breathing tests
options.D: Catching latent infections before they become active and contagious

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and treatment of existing disease, not genetic modification or primary prevention of DNA mutations. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h5)

question: When is the very first (baseline) needle count done during a procedure?

options.A: When the patient is rolling out of the recovery room
options.B: After the surgeon has closed the skin incision
options.C: Before the surgery begins during instrument setup
options.D: Only when an emergency X-ray is requested

question: When should you perform a secondary survey on a critically ill patient?

options.A: Only when the patient requests discharge
options.B: After immediate life threats are managed
options.C: At the very beginning of the primary survey
options.D: Before checking the airway or breathing

question: What is the safest way to check a patient's identity before starting an IV?

options.A: Look at the medication chart resting on the bedside table

options.C: Check the client's identification band using two unique identifiers

question: Which material is most commonly used to make everyday condoms?

options.A: Cotton
options.B: Silicone
options.C: Leather
options.D: Latex

question: How do you put together a complete nutritional care plan as a nurse?

options.A: By matching the patient's height to standard insurance weight charts
options.B: By combining data from all assessment categories to identify actual problems
options.C: By relying exclusively on the results of the 24-hour dietary recall
options.D: By prescribing high-dose vitamin supplements for every admitted patient

explanation: A solid care plan brings together physical checks, labs, diet history, and social findings to find the real root of the issue.

question: A rural clinic nurse finds that many women prefer giving birth at home. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Engage community leaders and educate women on the safety of facility delivery
options.B: Report all pregnant women who plan home births to the local police
options.C: Close the clinic until the women agree to come in voluntarily
options.D: Ignore the practice since home delivery has no real risks

question: Why are Environmental Health Officers so important to the primary healthcare team?

options.A: They handle all financial audits for the local health authority
options.B: They prescribe medications for chronic non-communicable diseases
options.C: They prevent disease by managing water, sanitation, and hygiene
options.D: They substitute for nurses during severe staff shortages

explanation: They tackle the root causes of sickness by making sure water sources are clean, surroundings are sanitary, and hygiene practices are up to standard.

question: How do informal mutual aid systems help support formal healthcare?

options.A: By filling gaps where government health resources cannot reach
options.B: By paying monthly salaries to all hospital nurses
options.C: By replacing all doctors with traditional herbal healers
options.D: By manufacturing advanced surgical equipment locally

question: What is the main focus of gerontological nursing?

options.A: Managing acute surgical emergencies in adults
options.B: Researching infectious disease outbreaks globally
options.C: Treating chronic diseases unique to childhood
options.D: Providing care specifically for older adults

question: Why does a drop in estrogen after menopause put women at higher risk for bone fractures?

options.A: Low hormone levels make the kidneys excrete all available vitamin D.

question: What is true about getting valid informed consent from a patient?

options.A: It is only necessary if the research involves major surgical procedures

options.C: It involves clear communication and genuine voluntary agreement, not just a signature
options.D: It can be waived by the nurse if the patient looks too tired to read

explanation: You got it! Consent isn't just about ticking a box or signing a paper—it's an ongoing conversation where the patient truly understands and freely agrees to take part.

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way for a nurse to handle referral barriers?

question: You are about to give an oral pill, but the chart says the drug should be given intravenously (IV). What do you do?

question: Why are home-based antenatal visits especially helpful for women living in rural areas?

options.A: It completely removes the risk of any pregnancy complication
options.B: It ensures the mother delivers at home every single time
options.C: It overcomes the barrier of long-distance travel to health facilities

question: Which patient in a busy emergency ward should a nurse monitor with a pulse oximeter first?

options.A: A patient with a mild ankle sprain from a football game

options.C: A patient waiting to be discharged after a healed minor cut

question: What is the main reason for keeping vaccines cold in a cold chain during transport and storage?

options.A: To stop healthcare workers from accidentally losing the vials

question: Which member of the healthcare team is a medical doctor who specializes in physical medicine and rehab?

question: What is the body's main use for carbohydrates?

options.C: Transporting fat-soluble vitamins through blood
options.D: Providing a quick and primary source of energy

question: What might you notice in an infant if the mother consumes too much caffeine?

options.D: Rapid whitening of the fingernails

question: What type of tissue lines the part of the urethra closest to the bladder?

options.C: Simple squamous epithelium
options.D: Transitional epithelium

question: A patient with severe arthritis cannot walk to the bathroom or manage clothing buttons fast enough, resulting in accidental urine loss. What type of incontinence is this?

options.A: Overflow incontinence
options.B: Urge incontinence
options.C: Functional incontinence
options.D: Stress incontinence

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main duties when it comes to environmental health?

options.A: Paving dirt roads to prevent dust inhalation in villages
options.B: Manufacturing chemical disinfectants in pharmaceutical labs
options.C: Educating patients and communities on hygiene practices

question: What is the big advantage of using topical haemostatic agents during surgery?

options.A: They control bleeding right at the specific wound site

options.C: They cure inherited blood disorders permanently
options.D: They thin the blood throughout the entire body

question: Which symptom means a patient with diarrhoea should stop home treatment and see a doctor right away?

options.A: Mild rumbling sounds in the abdomen
options.B: Blood appearing in the stool
options.C: Mild fatigue after a long day
options.D: A slight drop in appetite

question: What is a major safety worry when giving hypnotic medications to elderly patients?

options.A: Sudden permanent blindness upon waking

options.C: Rapid development of severe bone fractures

question: Which local group is often leveraged in Nigeria to help drive public health campaigns like immunization?

question: How do coenzymes help out enzymes?

options.D: By helping transfer chemical groups or electrons during reactions

question: What is the main goal of diagnostic testing for hormone (endocrine) disorders?

options.A: To destroy overactive hormone-producing tissue
options.B: To permanently replace missing organ functions
options.C: To cure infectious agents causing gland failure
options.D: To measure hormone levels and check organ response

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

question: What materials are modern contraceptive diaphragms usually made of?

options.A: Silicone or latex
options.B: Rigid hard plastic
options.C: Absorbable collagen
options.D: Woven cotton mesh

question: Which of these actions is an example of environmental source reduction to prevent malaria?

options.C: Treating infected patients with intravenous fluid therapy

question: When cleaning a patient's skin before surgery, what is the correct way to apply the antiseptic solution?

question: Which of these methods is NOT a reliable way to make water safe from amoebic cysts?

question: How does tucking the chin down to the chest help a patient who has trouble swallowing?

question: Which health problem is most often caused by poor ergonomic design at work?

options.A: Sudden bacterial pneumonia

options.C: Musculoskeletal disorders and chronic back pain
options.D: Acute viral gastroenteritis and food poisoning

question: What special feature helps cardiac muscle cells connect and pass electrical signals quickly?

options.C: Multiple peripheral nuclei
options.D: Lack of striations

question: Which enzyme in your saliva starts breaking down carbohydrates right in your mouth?

options.B: Salivary amylase

question: What should nurses do regarding swab counts during an emergency surgery?

options.C: It confirms that ovulation has already taken place.
options.D: It predicts the exact hour ovulation will happen today.

explanation: Because the slight temperature jump is driven by progesterone *after* release, BBT charting is great for confirming ovulation happened, rather than predicting it ahead of time.

question: A patient has a deep, suspicious mole that needs to be completely removed with a clear border of healthy skin. Which method is best?

options.A: Shave biopsy
options.B: Punch biopsy core
options.C: Excisional biopsy
options.D: Superficial scraping

explanation: An excisional biopsy takes out the entire lesion plus a small safety margin of healthy skin around it—great when we need total removal, like checking for melanoma.

question: When do modern recovery guidelines generally suggest starting food by mouth after surgery?

options.A: Only after 48 hours of complete fasting
options.B: Within hours of waking from anesthesia
options.C: After waiting for active bowel sounds
options.D: Only after the patient passes flatus

explanation: Spot on! Feeding patients early is safe and actually helps their bowels wake up faster than starving them for days.

question: Which workplace strategy shows that a hospital truly cares about long-term staff motivation?

options.A: Sponsoring specialty certifications and clear career ladders
options.B: Lowering entry-level salaries to save money for equipment
options.C: Reducing annual vacation days to increase bedside coverage
options.D: Eliminating all staff meetings to maximize shift hours

explanation: When a hospital helps you grow your skills and gives you clear paths to climb higher, you feel valued and ready to stay!

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To reduce maternal illness and death from abortion complications
options.B: To provide permanent sterilization to all female patients
options.C: To investigate the legal circumstances of a pregnancy loss
options.D: To promote mandatory reporting of all spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: Great job! PAC is all about saving lives and treating any physical or emotional issues after a pregnancy loss so the patient can recover safely.

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like right around the time of ovulation?

options.A: Thin and watery with a strong foul odor
options.B: Dry, crumbly, and dark brown in color
options.C: Clear, stretchy, and slippery like raw egg whites
options.D: Thick, sticky, and opaque like paste

explanation: High estrogen makes fertile mucus stretchy and slippery—just like raw egg white—to help sperm swim up easily. Nature is amazing!

question: A patient wants to leave the ward early because they cannot afford their remaining hospital bill. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Connect the patient with the hospital social welfare unit or available support schemes
options.B: Threaten to call security if the patient attempts to leave the bed
options.C: Ignore the situation since financial matters are strictly administrative
options.D: Pay the hospital bill directly out of the nurse's personal salary

explanation: Well done! Hospital social workers are there to help bridge financial gaps and find workable payment solutions so patients can finish their care safely.

question: What important safety advice should a nurse give a patient about stopping anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Stop taking them right away if your mouth feels dry
options.B: Reduce the dose slowly as advised by your doctor
options.C: Crush all the tablets so they clear your system faster
options.D: Double the dose if your tremors start coming back

explanation: You've got it! Stopping these meds suddenly can cause rebound muscle stiffness and make tremors flare up fiercely. Always taper safely!

question: Which antibodies are naturally present in the plasma of a person with Type A blood?

options.A: Anti-B antibodies
options.B: Anti-A antibodies
options.C: No ABO antibodies at all
options.D: Both anti-A and anti-B antibodies

explanation: Type A blood has A antigens on the cells, so the body develops anti-B antibodies to attack foreign B types. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why is addressing emotional and mental health considered essential in rehabilitative care?

options.A: Mental health support can reverse genetic mutations in the brain
options.B: Psychological counseling replaces the need for physical exercises
options.C: Emotional distress can worsen physical symptoms and reduce coping
options.D: Families do not require any support until the final stages of illness

explanation: Mental and emotional health directly impacts a patient's willingness and ability to participate in rehabilitation and enjoy daily life. You've got this!

question: Which objective of health education deals with building practical self-care skills like handwashing?

options.A: Cognitive objective
options.B: Affective objective
options.C: Psychodynamic objective
options.D: Administrative objective

explanation: The psychodynamic (or behavioral) objective focuses on the physical execution of practical skills—getting hands-on with procedures like wound care.

question: When is the best time to discuss family planning options with a patient receiving post-abortion care?

options.A: Before the patient is discharged from the clinical setting
options.B: Only after the patient experiences a second unplanned pregnancy
options.C: Refer them to a distant pharmacy without discussing options
options.D: Wait until six months have passed to avoid overwhelming them

explanation: Spot on! Bringing up family planning before discharge ensures the patient is protected against a quick repeat pregnancy while they are still connected to care.

question: Why do certain smells instantly trigger strong memories or emotions?

options.A: Smell signals pass through the visual cortex first
options.B: The nose shares a direct blood supply with the hippocampus
options.C: Odorants directly stimulate the motor strip in the frontal lobe
options.D: Olfactory pathways connect directly to the limbic system in the brain

explanation: You got it! Unlike other senses, smell signals bypass the brain's relay station (the thalamus) and go straight to emotional centers like the amygdala and hippocampus. That's why a scent can instantly remind you of home!

question: Why aren't standard antibody blood tests ideal for diagnosing an active case of onchocerciasis?

options.A: They only work during the first week of a bite
options.B: They require frozen tissue samples to function
options.C: They show past exposure rather than current infection
options.D: They cannot detect any immune response in humans

explanation: Antibodies stick around in the blood long after the body has dealt with the parasite. A positive blood test just means past exposure, not necessarily an active worm load right now.

question: How does the lower oesophageal sphincter keep itself tightly closed to stop acid reflux?

options.A: By active mucus production sealing the lower mucosal folds together
options.B: Through intrinsic smooth muscle tone reinforced by the diaphragmatic crura
options.C: By voluntary contraction of skeletal muscle fibers wrapped around the hiatus
options.D: Through continuous parasympathetic stimulation sent by the glossopharyngeal nerve

explanation: You got it! It relies on its own natural muscle tension plus a helpful extra squeeze from the diaphragm opening it passes through.

question: Which complication should a nurse watch for most closely right after a hysterectomy?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Sudden visual impairment
options.C: Hemorrhage and infection
options.D: Severe joint contractures

explanation: Spot on! Right after surgery, watching out for heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) and signs of infection is top priority.

question: What is the main job of freshwater snails in the life cycle of schistosomes?

options.A: They transport the parasite permanently out of aquatic environments.
options.B: They consume human waste to reduce overall environmental egg counts.
options.C: They serve as the definitive host where adult worms reproduce sexually.
options.D: They act as intermediate hosts where asexual multiplication occurs.

explanation: Think of the snail as a busy factory! Inside the snail, a single parasite multiplies into thousands of infectious cercariae. Neat biology fact for your clinical notes!

question: Which vital sign signs are classic for someone with uncontrolled hyperthyroidism?

options.A: Bradycardia and weak pulse
options.B: Tachycardia and bounding pulse
options.C: Severe hypotension and slow respirations
options.D: Normal heart rate with low temperature

explanation: Everything is running in fast-forward with hyperthyroidism! The heart pumps faster (tachycardia) and stronger, giving you that bounding pulse.

question: Why do infectious disease outbreaks often require international teamwork?

options.A: Infectious diseases easily cross national borders and spread globally
options.B: International agencies hold the patent on all known antibiotics
options.C: Local hospitals refuse to treat contagious patients
options.D: National governments lack any interest in stopping local outbreaks

explanation: Viruses and bacteria don't check passports at the border! Because germs spread fast across countries, countries must work together to stop pandemics.

question: What is the main job of agencies like NEMA and SEMA in Nigeria?

options.A: To manage hospital nursing shifts and patient charts
options.B: To construct residential housing in safe urban zones
options.C: To coordinate emergency management, warnings, and disaster response
options.D: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for public clinics

explanation: You got it! These agencies bring together planning, warnings, and relief efforts across the country.

question: A patient skips buying blood pressure meds because they have no cash, relying on herbs instead. What is the biggest danger of relying solely on out-of-pocket spending?

options.A: Better compliance with long-term medication schedules
options.B: Immediate financial relief and permanent cure of the hypertension
options.C: Automatic enrollment into the state health insurance scheme
options.D: Delayed care and increased risk of severe complications like stroke

explanation: Sad but true. When people have to pay cash upfront for everything, they often skip treatment, which can lead to life-threatening emergencies like strokes.

question: What determines when a wrapped sterile instrument pack officially expires and needs re-sterilization?

options.A: The exact number of days marked on the calendar
options.B: Damage, wetness, or a tear in the packaging barrier
options.C: Whether the autoclave machine was washed this week
options.D: The brand name of the paper wrap used by the hospital

explanation: Sterility is event-related; packs stay sterile indefinitely unless the protective packaging is compromised by moisture, dirt, or physical damage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: Around how many weeks of pregnancy do morning sickness and nausea usually start?

options.A: 1 to 3 weeks
options.B: 16 to 18 weeks
options.C: 10 to 12 weeks
options.D: 4 to 6 weeks

explanation: You will often see this early in the first trimester around weeks 4 to 6, right when hormones start shooting up. Great job keeping this in mind for antenatal care!

question: A student gets a sudden feeling of dread thinking about an upcoming exam next week. What is the best nursing term for this feeling?

options.A: Agoraphobia
options.B: Anxiety
options.C: Panic attack
options.D: Phobia

explanation: Anxiety is that generalized feeling of worry about future events. Unlike a specific, sudden trigger, it's just your mind working overtime about what's ahead!

question: What special enzyme do ringworm and other fungus types use to break into the outer skin layers?

options.A: Keratinase
options.B: Bradykinin
options.C: Collagenase
options.D: Histamine

explanation: Dermatophytic fungi release keratinase, an enzyme that literally digests the tough keratin protein found in your outer skin, hair, and nails.

question: What is the main goal of medication reconciliation during a patient's hospital stay?

options.A: To reduce the number of nurses required on duty
options.B: To return unused drugs back to the pharmaceutical company
options.C: To calculate the total cost of drugs used in the ward
options.D: To compare past and current medications to prevent errors

explanation: Medication reconciliation ensures that home medications and new hospital orders match properly without dangerous gaps or overlaps. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why do many community farming systems encourage seed saving?

options.A: To ensure that all seeds are patented by international corporations
options.B: To preserve climate-resilient seed varieties instead of buying commercial hybrids
options.C: To increase the overall cost of planting basic vegetables
options.D: To prevent any crops from growing during the dry season

explanation: You got it! Saving seeds helps farmers keep traditional, hardy crops growing locally without always having to buy expensive commercial seeds.

question: Which layer of the uterine wall is responsible for contractions during labor?

options.A: Epimetrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Perimetrium

explanation: The myometrium is made of smooth muscle tissue that contracts forcefully to push the baby out during childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h3)

question: What are the three Greek root words that make up the word epidemiology?

options.A: Eco, demos, and therapy
options.B: Epi, genos, and lysis
options.C: Epi, demos, and logos
options.D: Endo, pathos, and bios

explanation: You've got this! The term breaks down nicely: epi means 'upon', demos means 'people', and logos means 'study'. Together, they form the study of health events affecting populations.

question: A patient is worried about using modern contraceptives because of her religion. As a nurse, what is the best way to respond?

options.A: Provide respectful, non-judgmental counseling that acknowledges her values
options.B: Report her concerns to the hospital administration immediately
options.C: Tell her that her religious beliefs are outdated and incorrect
options.D: Refuse to discuss any options other than surgical sterilization

explanation: Always meet patients where they are! Good nurses respect personal values and give compassionate, supportive guidance without judgment.

question: What is the biggest danger of pouring leftover chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.A: The chemical instantly turns into a harmless gas
options.B: Labels become permanently stamped into the plastic
options.C: People may accidentally drink the toxic chemical
options.D: The plastic material dissolves within a few hours

explanation: You got it! Putting chemicals in drink bottles is a recipe for disaster because it tricks anyone—especially thirsty children—into thinking it's safe juice or water.

question: In nursing management, what do we mean by conflict "antecedents"?

options.A: The official disciplinary policies used after a fight occurs
options.B: The underlying conditions that create fertile ground for disputes
options.C: The emotional reactions patients have to hospital staff
options.D: The legal documents signed when a nurse is hired

explanation: Think of antecedents as the early sparks or background conditions that set the stage for a disagreement to happen later. Spotting them early helps you keep the ward peaceful!

question: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks comes in with a fully infibulated Type III FGM scar. What is the best clinical approach?

options.A: Advise her to deliver completely unassisted at home
options.B: Plan for an antenatal or intrapartum defibulation procedure
options.C: Wait until pushing begins without any clinical preparation
options.D: Perform an immediate emergency hysterectomy

explanation: You nailed it! Planning ahead for defibulation lets the birth canal open safely before or during labor, preventing severe tears and fetal distress. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of these body areas is a classic, go-to site for giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: The sole of the foot
options.B: The abdomen
options.C: The center of the chest
options.D: The palm of the hand

explanation: That's right! The abdomen is a favorite spot for everyday injections like insulin and heparin because it has a nice, accessible layer of fat.

question: A patient who just had major vulval surgery is crying and refuses to look at her wound. What is your best first response?

options.A: Contact the surgeon to prescribe a strong antipsychotic medication
options.B: Provide a compassionate, listening ear and validate her feelings
options.C: Tell her that the scars are completely normal and she should be happy
options.D: Force her to look at the wound immediately to speed up acceptance

explanation: Spot on! Changes to intimate body parts cause deep emotional pain. Sitting down to listen and validate her feelings builds vital trust.

question: Why should standard cloth or fabric tailors' tapes be avoided in clinical practice?

options.A: They only measure in inches rather than centimeters
options.B: They are too expensive for community clinics
options.C: They stretch over time and give false readings
options.D: They dissolve easily when exposed to skin moisture

explanation: Fabric stretches with repeated pulling, which ruins the accuracy required for precise health tracking. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h2)

question: How is menopause officially diagnosed in a patient?

options.A: Surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.B: A sudden spike in body temperature
options.C: Complete stop of pituitary hormones
options.D: Twelve straight months without a menstrual period

explanation: You got it! Clinicians look back and confirm menopause once a woman has gone a full 12 months without any bleeding.

question: What is the biggest flaw in relying too strictly on the Kubler-Ross stages?

options.A: Grief is not a rigid, universal checklist
options.B: It was proven false by lab blood tests
options.C: Patients never experience anger or depression
options.D: It only works for children with cancer

explanation: Every patient handles grief differently. Treating these stages like strict rules can make us miss the person right in front of us.

question: Which embryonic germ layer gives rise to the nervous system and skin?

options.A: Trophoblast
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: Think 'ecto' for outer—the outer layer builds things that face the outside world, like your skin and your brain/nerves!
